- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for short-term (1–7d) to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 20–40% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 5–15% in first 2–3 days of sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates by 20–50% in all examples; apply a 30d decay factor (e.g., multiply by 0.6–0.7) to reduce long-term bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to overshoot recovery; cap forecast at 1.2x recent peak for 5–7d horizon.
